label: PF Backlog 578
title: Eventing SSOT (Go): event core - append-only store, emit, monotonic seq, cursor/since
body:
## Problem / why
The canonical stream has no reliable cursor (since = string timestamp compare) and no Go-native core; new
shipped logic must be Go.

## Goal / value
A Go event core owning emit + append-only store + monotonic seq + cursor reads; single writer.

## In scope
- Go package (extend go/pfcore or new go/eventbus) with emit/seq/cursor; single-writer store.
- Invoked from Python via core/go_host + A1 wire (fail-closed).

## Out of scope
- Dispatch/transports (E4/E5); changing existing Python emit call sites (E7).

## Acceptance criteria
- Monotonic seq assigned; cursor read returns exactly events after a cursor (no races).
- Existing events.jsonl readers still work; no duplicate store introduced.

## Verification / test plan
- Go unit tests + Python contract/e2e test; language_rule_check green.

decisions.decision: Add event append/read ops to go/pfcore via the A1 wire; Python stays writer until 1272; portable lockfile for append+seq

decisions.note: HIL approved Gate 1; design findings actioned.
Gate 1 re-approved: owner correction only (PG event store in go/edpdata; pfcore A1 seam).

brief.problem:
The canonical stream has no reliable cursor (since = string timestamp compare) and no Go-native core; new
shipped logic must be Go.
brief.what_adds: A Go event core owning emit + append-only store + monotonic seq + cursor reads; single writer.
brief.why:
The canonical stream has no reliable cursor (since = string timestamp compare) and no Go-native core; new
shipped logic must be Go.

objective: A Go event core owning emit + append-only store + monotonic seq + cursor reads; single writer.
acceptance_criteria: Go event core appends events to PostgreSQL with a per-tenant monotonic seq and an outbox row in the same transaction; cursor reads return exactly events with seq greater than the cursor.
Large event payloads are stored in object storage; PostgreSQL stores only opaque ref, sha256, size and content type, and emit fails closed if storage fails.
events.jsonl becomes a read-only compatibility projection; existing readers keep working and no second event authority or dual writer exists.
Outbox writes are feature-flagged off/bounded until BI-PF-1269 dispatcher ships, with observable row-count limits.
in_scope: Go package (extend go/pfcore or new go/eventbus) with emit/seq/cursor; single-writer store.
Invoked from Python via core/go_host + A1 wire (fail-closed).
out_of_scope: Dispatch/transports (E4/E5); changing existing Python emit call sites (E7).
approach: - Go unit tests + Python contract/e2e test; language_rule_check green.

prior_decisions: ADR-0005: Go core owns store+emit+seq+cursor; Python thin client; single writer; A1 seam; extend go/pfcore first (Q1)
BI-PF-1267: event-envelope contract (schema) defined; wire-request op enum = ping/describe/validate/canonicalize
core/events.py:1-11 is the single writer of events.jsonl (Python) until the 1272 cutover (Q4)
core/go_host.py: stateless one-shot subprocess seam (stdin/stdout), fail-closed, builds the binary on demand
ADR-0001: new shipped/sensitive logic -> Go under go/; no new Python modules in core/
existing_path: Go host + op dispatch -> go/pfcore/pfcore.go Handle; main.go reads one wire-request
wire contract + op enum -> core/contracts.py (_WIRE_REQUEST) + go/contract + go/pfcore mirrors
event store (SSOT) -> products/<project>/events.jsonl via core/events.py + core/log_router
portable exclusive lock pattern -> core/worker.py:84-105 (O_CREAT|O_EXCL lockfile)
invocation -> core/go_host.invoke(op, contract_name, payload, req_id, source)
assumptions: C1 event ops are added to go/pfcore (not a separate binary) by extending the wire-request op enum (additive)
C2 the stateless Go core receives the store path in the payload (it does not know ROOT)
C3 during 1268 Python REMAINS the writer (no dual write); Go ops are exercised by tests + available via go_host; the emit-path cutover is 1272
C4 portable exclusive lock (O_CREATE|O_EXCL lockfile, mirroring core/worker) for append+seq; stdlib-only Go (no new deps)
C5 monotonic seq = last persisted seq + 1 under the lock (sidecar counter only if needed)
divergences: extending the frozen wire-request op enum is a contract change -> recorded as a decision (additive; both Go mirrors + parity test)
a Go writer alongside the Python writer would break single-writer -> explicitly avoided until the 1272 cutover
open_questions: Q1 op shape: discrete ops (event_append/event_read) vs one 'events' op with an action field
Q2 wiring for 1268: ops exercised by tests + reachable via go_host (dormant on the emit path) vs feature-flagged call
Q3 seq source: last-line+1 vs a sidecar counter file
Q4 store scope/path passed by the caller (product_forge root vs product dir)
Q5 ownership: 1268 builds+exposes the core; the Python cutover stays 1272 (no overlap)

impact_review.evidence: core/contracts.py _WIRE_REQUEST; go/contract + pfcore mirrors; parity test

impact_review.claim: Python remains the writer (no dual write)
Stateless core takes store path in payload

evidence:
Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=deb5b55ac4d2
BLOCKER:
  - AC-3 cannot be met as specified: Go becomes sole writer to PostgreSQL but no in-scope component regenerates the read-only events.jsonl, so legacy readers silently receive stale data (projection "refresh" trigger has no owner in affected_files).
MAJOR:
  - Per-tenant seq uniqueness not stated as a constraint; design only lists index (tenant_id, seq), allowing concurrent appends to race and produce duplicate seq, breaking AC-1's "exactly events seq>cursor" guarantee.
  - Migration 0024 down path drops the event authority table (destructive, non-reversible without data loss); no verified backup/restore checkpoint is defined before applying/reverting it (checklist item 1).
  - CL-011 unaddressed: no design evidence or test that the runtime DB role is NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS and remains subject to FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on events/outbox.
  - Outbox row-count bound (AC-4) has no enforcing owner or cleanup job before BI-PF-1269; an alert alone does not bound rows, so "observable row-count limits" degrade to unbounded growth.
  - Object-store orphan cleanup is listed as a guardrail but has no owner, test, or acceptance evidence in the declared files, risking unrecoverable garbage and cost growth.
MINOR:
  - `risks` field is "Not specified." despite a cross-item cutover (1266/1267/1269) with a migration and writer swap; risk register should be populated before Gate 1.5.
  - Failure matrix error codes (EVENT_OUTBOX_UNBOUNDED, projection stale) have no corresponding metric/log contract test in the listed test files.
  - Rollback text is only "Revert the change"; it does not state recovery from a migration-interrupted state (checklist item 6).
NIT:
  - Traceability maps FR-4→AC-3 while AC-3 is JSONL and FR-3 is cursor; AC/FR numbering in coverage rows should be reconciled to avoid audit confusion.
SUMMARY:
  - The Go-authority direction is sound and language-rule compliant, but AC-3 is not deliverable without an owned projection producer, and AC-1/AC-4 hinge on unstated uniqueness/bound enforcement. Top risks: stale legacy reads after cutover, duplicate per-tenant seq under concurrency, and unbounded outbox/orphan growth.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

BLOCKER:

MAJOR:

  - test_matrix evidence cites go/pfcore/event_projection_test.go, which is not in review_scope.files; evidence outside declared scope cannot be verified at this gate.
  - Failure-matrix error codes (EVENT_OUTBOX_UNBOUNDED, projection stale) still have no corresponding metric/log contract test in the listed test files (residual; observability rows changed).

  - Traceability FR-4→AC-3 mismatch and unspecified `risks` field persist unchanged and remain as previously logged.
RECOMMENDATION: no hard blocker (MAJOR/MINOR/NIT advisory; HIL decides)

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=d795e655e201
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - Delta adds "prune job enforces bound" (failure_matrix + guardrails) but never states whether pruning may delete *pending* outbox rows; with no dispatcher until BI-PF-1269, bound-enforcement-by-deletion silently drops undelivered dispatch intent (AC-4 data-loss risk).
  - New controls added to design_pack coverage/test_matrix (outbox prune, payload GC, RLS posture tests) have no matching functional_spec.traceability/requirements rows in the same delta, violating the delta rule that control/test changes update matching design rows and evidence.
MINOR:
  - EVENT_MIGRATION_BACKUP_REQUIRED appears in the delta failure_matrix but has no owner, coverage row, or test evidence anywhere in the declared review_scope files; "refuse downgrade unless verified backup" is unenforced at this gate (checklist items 1 and 6).
  - test_matrix contains near-duplicate AC-4 prune rows ("outbox prune/bound" → eventstore_pg_test.go vs "outbox prune bound" → event_outbox_prune_test.go), leaving evidence mapping ambiguous for the same control.
  - functional_spec in the delta is effectively identical to the previously approved content, so no FR-level contract was updated to absorb the new prune/GC/RLS controls added in design_pack.
NIT:
  - none
SUMMARY:
  - Delta materially closes prior gaps: EVENT_OUTBOX_DISABLED now states flag-off append behavior, and prune/GC/RLS gain coverage, test, and ownership rows.
  - Top residual risks: bound enforcement may destroy pending outbox rows before BI-PF-1269, and new test evidence is not mirrored into functional_spec traceability in this delta.
  - Recommend resolving the prune retention semantics (alert/block pending rows vs delete delivered only) before Gate 1.5.
RECOMMENDATION: no hard blocker (MAJOR/MINOR/NIT advisory; HIL decides)

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=1bfb2402407f
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - none
MINOR:
  - New failure_matrix row EVENT_OUTBOX_BOUND_EXCEEDED mandates "enable backpressure", but config_contract defines only EVENT_INLINE_PAYLOAD_LIMIT/EVENT_OUTBOX_ENABLED; no backpressure knob or owner is specified, so the control is unimplementable as written.
  - FR-1/FR-2 `requirements[].verification` still point solely to eventstore_pg_test.go while new controls (outbox prune, payload GC) are owned by 1268; requirements rows were not updated in this delta even though traceability was.

RECOMMENDATION: no hard blocker (MAJOR/MINOR/NIT advisory; HIL decides)

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=86ea3ecb0516
BLOCKER:
  - AC-2 unimplemented: `Append` always writes `payload` inline to PostgreSQL; no object-store upload path, no `EVENT_INLINE_PAYLOAD_LIMIT` threshold, no `payload_ref`/`sha256` population, no fail-closed `EVENT_PAYLOAD_STORE_FAILED` path.
  - AC-3 unmet: `RegenerateProjection` has zero call sites; when `PF_DB_DSN` is set the writer stops appending to `events.jsonl` while nothing regenerates it, so existing JSONL readers observe stale/empty data (readers do not keep working).
  - AC-3/AC-4 evidence files declared in scope are absent from the diff: `go/edpdata/event_projection_test.go`, `test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_event_core.py`, and all `eventstore_pg_test.go` traceability evidence — no fail-able test for projection, outbox flag/bound, RLS posture, or concurrency.
  - AC-4 unmet: no observable outbox row-count limit, metric, or alert anywhere; `PruneOutbox` exists but nothing enforces/bounds/observes pending-row growth while the dispatcher is absent.
  - Data loss (cross-tenant): `PayloadStore.List(ctx)` takes no tenant scope, so `ReconcilePayloads` for tenant A computes "unreferenced" from A's RLS-filtered view and deletes tenant B's objects; `Delete` is also unscoped.
  - Security: `EVENT_OUTBOX_ENABLED` invalid values (e.g. `yes`, `1`) are silently treated as off by `EqualFold(...,"on")`, violating the config contract's fail-closed `invalid_behavior`.
MAJOR:
  - Seq allocation uses `SELECT MAX(seq)+1` with no lock and no retry on unique conflict (design requires retry) — concurrent appends to one tenant collide on PK `(tenant_id,seq)` and fail; no concurrency test exists.
  - `EventAppendOp`/`EventReadOp` open and close a full PostgreSQL pool per request via `OpenEventStoreFromEnv` with `context.Background()` (no timeout/cancel) — scalability and SPOF risk at the A1 seam.
  - Payload GC TOCTOU: objects uploaded but whose event row is not yet committed (or whose append later rolls back) are deleted immediately; no grace window / `created_at` age filter before `Delete`.
  - Zero observability emitted: no append latency/error metrics, outbox row count/lag, cursor lag, prune/GC results, or projection age despite the design's observability contract.
  - `fmt.Sprint(ev["event_id"])` turns a missing field into literal `"<nil>"`, which passes `Append` validation — malformed events are persisted with bogus ids/types.
  - CL-011 role-posture evidence missing: no test proving NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS runtime role under `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`.
MINOR:
  - `Read` does not reject future/unknown cursors (`EVENT_CURSOR_INVALID` per failure matrix); returns empty page instead.
  - `RegenerateProjection` buffers all events in memory (unbounded), writes no staleness marker/age, and never verifies JSONL permissions are read-only for consumers.
  - Duplicate `event_id` returns a raw driver error instead of an idempotent replay response (FR idempotency/edge case "retry duplicate").
  - Destructive down-migration backup refusal is a comment only — no enforced checkpoint verification (`EVENT_MIGRATION_BACKUP_REQUIRED`).
  - `mustJSON` discards marshal errors, silently encoding invalid payloads.
  - Flag/env reads (`PF_DB_DSN`, `EVENT_OUTBOX_ENABLED`) are re-read per request with no startup validation as required by the config contract.
NIT:
  - Projection temp file `path + ".tmp"` is not unique — concurrent regenerations can clobber each other.
  - `PruneOutbox` wraps a single DELETE in a transaction solely to set tenant/timeout.
  - `ReconcilePayloads` returns a partial `deleted` count alongside an error, which callers may misread as success.
  - `go.mod` jumps `go 1.21` → `go 1.25.0` without note; confirm toolchain alignment with repo standard.
SUMMARY:
  - The diff establishes a plausible PostgreSQL event store skeleton (RLS, atomic event+outbox, cursor read) but ships none of AC-2, only dead code for AC-3, and no bounds/observability for AC-4 — three of four acceptance criteria are demonstrably unmet, with declared test evidence files missing entirely.
  - Top risks: cross-tenant payload deletion in GC, silent JSONL reader starvation after cutover, concurrent seq conflicts without retry, and per-request connection churn at the A1 wire seam.
  - Verdict: not approvable; requires the object-storage emit path, a wired projection regeneration with tests, scoped/deferred payload GC, outbox bound + metrics, and seq-concurrency handling before Gate re-review.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=a38e7f93d541
BLOCKER:
  - AC-3/tenant isolation: `EventAppendOp` passes caller-supplied `payload["path"]` straight into `RegenerateProjection` (pfcore hunk), so any A1 caller can redirect the writer to another tenant's JSONL (or any writable path) and overwrite it — projection path must be server-resolved, not wire-controlled.
  - AC-2 fail-closed gap introduced by the delta: offload runs `payloads.Put` before any DB write and, if `WithPayloads` was never configured (`inlineLimit==0`), `Append` silently writes large payloads inline to PostgreSQL instead of failing closed per the config contract.
MAJOR:
  - AC-4: new `EnforceOutboxBound` has no production call site — it is not invoked by `Append`, no job, and emits no metric/log, so the row-count limit remains dead code and outbox growth stays unobservable.
  - AC-3 integrity: `RegenerateProjection` runs after the event transaction commits; a projection failure makes `event_append` report failure for an already-persisted event, and the client's retry then fails on duplicate `event_id` — inconsistent authority reporting.
  - AC-3: projection refresh is conditional on the caller including `path`; an append without it commits to PostgreSQL but never regenerates `events.jsonl`, so legacy readers silently go stale.
  - Seq-conflict detection uses `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "duplicate key")` — message/driver dependent and untested; a duplicate `event_id` is retried 5× pointlessly while non-`seq` unique violations also retrigger allocation.
MINOR:
  - `payloads.Put` precedes the transaction; a failed/aborted commit leaves an orphan object, and the new grace window only applies when callers pass `graceSeconds > 0` (existing test passes 0).
  - No fail-closed test for storage failure (`Put` error → `Append` error) or for sha256/size/content-type persistence in the row; `TestAppendUsesObjectStoreAboveThreshold` only asserts the ref string.
  - `TestOutboxBoundFailsClosed` asserts only `err != nil`, so an `ErrEventInvalid` validation failure would satisfy it instead of proving `ErrOutboxBound`.
  - Grace window silently degrades if a store returns `CreatedAt==0`: `now-0` always exceeds grace, so in-flight objects are deletable despite the TOCTOU guard.
  - `sharedEventStore` is an unclosable package-global (discarded `closeFn`), serializing all appends behind the first DB open and preventing clean shutdown/test reset.
  - [OUT_OF_SCOPE] `CorrelationID`/`CausationID`/`Actor`/`Version` still use `fmt.Sprint` and persist `"<nil>"` for missing fields; only `event_id`/`event_type` were fixed in this delta.
NIT:
  - Retry loop has no backoff/jitter across its 5 attempts under per-tenant seq contention.
  - Hard-coded 30s context timeout is not declared in the config contract (`EVENT_*` registry).
SUMMARY:
  - Delta resolves most prior blockers (payload offload path, tenant-scoped GC, fail-closed outbox flag, seq retry, pooled store, role-posture test), but introduces a wire-controlled projection path (cross-tenant overwrite risk) and leaves AC-4's new bound unwired and unobserved.
  - Top risks: caller-controlled `RegenerateProjection` path, post-commit projection failure corrupting append semantics, and `inlineLimit<=0` silently reverting to inline PG payloads.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=66ce76e2715a
BLOCKER:
  - AC-3/tenant isolation (pfcore hunk): when `PF_EVENT_PROJECTION_DIR` is set, `projPath := filepath.Join(projRoot, "events.jsonl")` drops the tenant segment entirely — the env is process-wide and cannot vary per tenant, so every tenant regenerates the *same* file and each append overwrites other tenants' projections (cross-tenant leak + lost projection). Tenant must be joined in both branches.
MAJOR:
  - AC-1 (eventstore.go hunk): retry match narrowed from `"duplicate key"` to `"events_pkey"`. The design mandates retry on the `UNIQUE(tenant_id, seq)` conflict, which is a *separate* constraint unless the PK is exactly `(tenant_id, seq)`; if not, concurrent seq conflicts now abort instead of retrying while PK duplicates retry 5×. No test proves the retry still fires for the actual seq constraint name.
  - AC-4 observability (delta touches this line): `EnforceOutboxBound` is now invoked, but the rejection still emits no metric/log/counter and the bound check itself produces no row-count signal, so operators cannot distinguish `EVENT_OUTBOX_BOUND_EXCEEDED` backpressure from a generic append failure.
MINOR:
  - Bound check runs *after* payload offload (`payloads.Put` precedes it): an outbox-bound rejection orphans an already-uploaded object and relies on GC grace; the cheap check should fail fast before the expensive write.
  - Per-append `EnforceOutboxBound` adds a DB round-trip (likely a COUNT over outbox) to every outbox-enabled append: O(pending rows) latency at scale, TOCTOU-racy outside the tx (bound advisory under concurrency), with no supporting index/metric evidence.
  - `WithOutboxBound` mutates the receiver in place (unsafe if applied to a shared/global store; post-construction config mutation) and silently ignores `<=0`, contradicting the config contract's `invalid_behavior: fail closed`.
  - New `TestAppendEnforcesOutboxBound` asserts only `err != nil`; an `ErrEventInvalid` or DB error would satisfy it — assert the specific bound error to prove AC-4 backpressure.
  - `NewEventStore` hard-codes `inlineLimit: 32*1024` / `outboxMax: 100_000` as magic numbers rather than sourcing the declared `EVENT_INLINE_PAYLOAD_LIMIT` / outbox bound from the config contract with startup validation (divergence risk between code and contract).
  - `PF_EVENT_PROJECTION_DIR` is a new env var read via `os.Getenv` per append, with no startup validation and no entry in the config contract or env registry.
  - Projection default root `filepath.Join("products", tenant)` is cwd-relative (a service started elsewhere writes where no reader looks, silently stale), and `tenant` is joined unsanitized — a tenant value containing a separator or `..` escapes the projection root.
NIT:
  - The outbox-bound test belongs in `eventstore_test.go`, not `event_outbox_gc_test.go`.
  - `projection_error` is surfaced only in the returned map; nothing logs/meters it, so AC-3 stale-projection marking depends entirely on callers echoing the field.
SUMMARY:
  - Delta correctly resolves the two prior blockers (caller-controlled projection path now server-resolved; large payload without store now fails closed) and wires `EnforceOutboxBound` into `Append`.
  - Top risks: the new `PF_EVENT_PROJECTION_DIR` branch drops tenant scoping (blocker), and narrowing the duplicate-match to `events_pkey` may disable the required per-tenant seq retry with no test evidence.
  - Remaining hardening: bound-check ordering/observability, config-registry alignment for new constants/env var, and stronger assertions in the new tests.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=0334907eb280
BLOCKER:
  - AC-3 regression (pfcore hunk): with `projRoot == ""` the code still sets `projRoot = filepath.Join("products", tenant)`, and the new line then joins `tenant` again — default writes become `products/<tenant>/<tenant>/events.jsonl`, so existing readers of `products/<tenant>/events.jsonl` silently stop receiving updates (stale projection).
MAJOR:
  - The tenant-path fix (disposition of prior BLOCKER) ships with no test in this delta: nothing asserts the env-set path `<dir>/<tenant>/events.jsonl` nor that the default path stays exactly where legacy readers look, so the double-tenant defect above is undetected by CI.
MINOR:

  - The retry hunk still matches constraint names by substring on `err.Error()` (`events_tenant_id_seq_key`); DB error-message coupling is brittle across PG versions/upgrades (pre-existing pattern, extended here).

  - The new log line duplicates the `pending=/max=` data already present in the returned error string.
SUMMARY:
  - Delta correctly targets all three prior pending findings, but the AC-3 tenant-path fix is wrong on the default branch (tenant joined twice), breaking legacy `events.jsonl` readers — a hard AC-3 regression.
  - Outbox bound logging and seq-conflict retry additions look correct but are untested in this delta.
  - Must fix path composition (append `tenant` only when `projRoot` comes from the env override) and add a regression test for both branches before merge.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=d625c603b93f
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - none
MINOR:
  - `projectionPath` joins the raw `tenant` into a filesystem path with no sanitization; a tenant value containing `..` or a separator can escape `PF_EVENT_PROJECTION_DIR`/`products` (tenant is server-resolved, so low likelihood, but this is a new path-construction helper and deserves a boundary assertion).
NIT:

SUMMARY:
  - Delta resolves the prior BLOCKER (double-tenant default path) and MAJOR (missing tests): `projectionPath` now yields `products/<tenant>/events.jsonl` by default and `<dir>/<tenant>/events.jsonl` under env, matching legacy reader locations, with both cases unit-tested.
  - Behavior under env-set root is byte-identical to the old code, so AC-3 reader compatibility is preserved; no new AC/security regression introduced.
  - Residual risk is limited to unsanitized tenant segment in the new path helper (MINOR hardening).
RECOMMENDATION: no hard blocker (MAJOR/MINOR/NIT advisory; HIL decides)

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing components/APIs: core/artifact_store.py, core/asset_store.py, core/events.py, core/event_bus.py

api_impact.reason: Internal A1 event seam only; no public API route change.

requirements: Go event core appends events to PostgreSQL with a per-tenant monotonic seq and an outbox row in the same transaction; cursor reads return exactly events with seq greater than the cursor.
Large event payloads are stored in object storage; PostgreSQL stores only opaque ref, sha256, size and content type, and emit fails closed if storage fails.
events.jsonl becomes a read-only compatibility projection; existing readers keep working and no second event authority or dual writer exists.
Outbox writes are feature-flagged off/bounded until BI-PF-1269 dispatcher ships, with observable row-count limits.
non_goals: No breaking change to existing event readers
invariants: PostgreSQL is the sole event authority.
seq is assigned per tenant in the DB transaction; no producer-supplied seq.
Events and outbox rows commit atomically.
Large payload bytes never live in PostgreSQL above threshold.

api: No public HTTP API change; A1 event_append/event_read seam preserved.

New controls added to design_pack coverage/test_matrix (outbox prune, payload GC, RLS posture tests) have no matching functional_spec.traceability/requirements rows in the same delta, violating the delta rule that control/test changes update matching design rows and evidence.

SUMMARY: Delta materially closes prior gaps: EVENT_OUTBOX_DISABLED now states flag-off append behavior, and prune/GC/RLS gain coverage, test, and ownership rows.

MINOR: New failure_matrix row EVENT_OUTBOX_BOUND_EXCEEDED mandates "enable backpressure", but config_contract defines only EVENT_INLINE_PAYLOAD_LIMIT/EVENT_OUTBOX_ENABLED; no backpressure knob or owner is specified, so the control is unimplementable as written.

FR-4 edge_case "PostgreSQL down" / error "Projection stale marked" does not state projection write atomicity (temp+rename) or staleness metric, though observability lists "projection age".
SUMMARY: Delta resolves the prior data-loss MAJOR: prune is now explicitly forbidden from deleting pending/claimed rows and the bound is enforced via backpressure/disable, preserving dispatch intent until BI-PF-1269.
Traceability rows now reference outbox-prune and payload-GC tests, partially closing the delta-rule mismatch, but FR requirements/verification rows remain stale.

BLOCKER: AC-2 unimplemented: `Append` always writes `payload` inline to PostgreSQL; no object-store upload path, no `EVENT_INLINE_PAYLOAD_LIMIT` threshold, no `payload_ref`/`sha256` population, no fail-closed `EVENT_PAYLOAD_STORE_FAILED` path.

AC-3 unmet: `RegenerateProjection` has zero call sites; when `PF_DB_DSN` is set the writer stops appending to `events.jsonl` while nothing regenerates it, so existing JSONL readers observe stale/empty data (readers do not keep working).

AC-3/AC-4 evidence files declared in scope are absent from the diff: `go/edpdata/event_projection_test.go`, `test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_event_core.py`, and all `eventstore_pg_test.go` traceability evidence — no fail-able test for projection, outbox flag/bound, RLS posture, or concurrency.
AC-4 unmet: no observable outbox row-count limit, metric, or alert anywhere; `PruneOutbox` exists but nothing enforces/bounds/observes pending-row growth while the dispatcher is absent.

Data loss (cross-tenant): `PayloadStore.List(ctx)` takes no tenant scope, so `ReconcilePayloads` for tenant A computes "unreferenced" from A's RLS-filtered view and deletes tenant B's objects; `Delete` is also unscoped.
Security: `EVENT_OUTBOX_ENABLED` invalid values (e.g. `yes`, `1`) are silently treated as off by `EqualFold(...,"on")`, violating the config contract's fail-closed `invalid_behavior`.
MAJOR: Seq allocation uses `SELECT MAX(seq)+1` with no lock and no retry on unique conflict (design requires retry) — concurrent appends to one tenant collide on PK `(tenant_id,seq)` and fail; no concurrency test exists.
`EventAppendOp`/`EventReadOp` open and close a full PostgreSQL pool per request via `OpenEventStoreFromEnv` with `context.Background()` (no timeout/cancel) — scalability and SPOF risk at the A1 seam.
Payload GC TOCTOU: objects uploaded but whose event row is not yet committed (or whose append later rolls back) are deleted immediately; no grace window / `created_at` age filter before `Delete`.
Zero observability emitted: no append latency/error metrics, outbox row count/lag, cursor lag, prune/GC results, or projection age despite the design's observability contract.
`fmt.Sprint(ev["event_id"])` turns a missing field into literal `"<nil>"`, which passes `Append` validation — malformed events are persisted with bogus ids/types.
CL-011 role-posture evidence missing: no test proving NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS runtime role under `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`.
MINOR: `Read` does not reject future/unknown cursors (`EVENT_CURSOR_INVALID` per failure matrix); returns empty page instead.
`RegenerateProjection` buffers all events in memory (unbounded), writes no staleness marker/age, and never verifies JSONL permissions are read-only for consumers.
Duplicate `event_id` returns a raw driver error instead of an idempotent replay response (FR idempotency/edge case "retry duplicate").
Destructive down-migration backup refusal is a comment only — no enforced checkpoint verification (`EVENT_MIGRATION_BACKUP_REQUIRED`).
`mustJSON` discards marshal errors, silently encoding invalid payloads.
Flag/env reads (`PF_DB_DSN`, `EVENT_OUTBOX_ENABLED`) are re-read per request with no startup validation as required by the config contract.
NIT: Projection temp file `path + ".tmp"` is not unique — concurrent regenerations can clobber each other.
`PruneOutbox` wraps a single DELETE in a transaction solely to set tenant/timeout.
`ReconcilePayloads` returns a partial `deleted` count alongside an error, which callers may misread as success.
`go.mod` jumps `go 1.21` → `go 1.25.0` without note; confirm toolchain alignment with repo standard.
SUMMARY: The diff establishes a plausible PostgreSQL event store skeleton (RLS, atomic event+outbox, cursor read) but ships none of AC-2, only dead code for AC-3, and no bounds/observability for AC-4 — three of four acceptance criteria are demonstrably unmet, with declared test evidence files missing entirely.
Top risks: cross-tenant payload deletion in GC, silent JSONL reader starvation after cutover, concurrent seq conflicts without retry, and per-request connection churn at the A1 wire seam.

Verdict: not approvable; requires the object-storage emit path, a wired projection regeneration with tests, scoped/deferred payload GC, outbox bound + metrics, and seq-concurrency handling before Gate re-review.

BLOCKER: AC-3/tenant isolation: `EventAppendOp` passes caller-supplied `payload["path"]` straight into `RegenerateProjection` (pfcore hunk), so any A1 caller can redirect the writer to another tenant's JSONL (or any writable path) and overwrite it — projection path must be server-resolved, not wire-controlled.

AC-2 fail-closed gap introduced by the delta: offload runs `payloads.Put` before any DB write and, if `WithPayloads` was never configured (`inlineLimit==0`), `Append` silently writes large payloads inline to PostgreSQL instead of failing closed per the config contract.
MAJOR: AC-4: new `EnforceOutboxBound` has no production call site — it is not invoked by `Append`, no job, and emits no metric/log, so the row-count limit remains dead code and outbox growth stays unobservable.

AC-3 integrity: `RegenerateProjection` runs after the event transaction commits; a projection failure makes `event_append` report failure for an already-persisted event, and the client's retry then fails on duplicate `event_id` — inconsistent authority reporting.
AC-3: projection refresh is conditional on the caller including `path`; an append without it commits to PostgreSQL but never regenerates `events.jsonl`, so legacy readers silently go stale.

Seq-conflict detection uses `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "duplicate key")` — message/driver dependent and untested; a duplicate `event_id` is retried 5× pointlessly while non-`seq` unique violations also retrigger allocation.
MINOR: `payloads.Put` precedes the transaction; a failed/aborted commit leaves an orphan object, and the new grace window only applies when callers pass `graceSeconds > 0` (existing test passes 0).
No fail-closed test for storage failure (`Put` error → `Append` error) or for sha256/size/content-type persistence in the row; `TestAppendUsesObjectStoreAboveThreshold` only asserts the ref string.
`TestOutboxBoundFailsClosed` asserts only `err != nil`, so an `ErrEventInvalid` validation failure would satisfy it instead of proving `ErrOutboxBound`.
Grace window silently degrades if a store returns `CreatedAt==0`: `now-0` always exceeds grace, so in-flight objects are deletable despite the TOCTOU guard.
`sharedEventStore` is an unclosable package-global (discarded `closeFn`), serializing all appends behind the first DB open and preventing clean shutdown/test reset.
[OUT_OF_SCOPE] `CorrelationID`/`CausationID`/`Actor`/`Version` still use `fmt.Sprint` and persist `"<nil>"` for missing fields; only `event_id`/`event_type` were fixed in this delta.
NIT: Retry loop has no backoff/jitter across its 5 attempts under per-tenant seq contention.
Hard-coded 30s context timeout is not declared in the config contract (`EVENT_*` registry).
SUMMARY: Delta resolves most prior blockers (payload offload path, tenant-scoped GC, fail-closed outbox flag, seq retry, pooled store, role-posture test), but introduces a wire-controlled projection path (cross-tenant overwrite risk) and leaves AC-4's new bound unwired and unobserved.
Top risks: caller-controlled `RegenerateProjection` path, post-commit projection failure corrupting append semantics, and `inlineLimit<=0` silently reverting to inline PG payloads.

BLOCKER: AC-3/tenant isolation (pfcore hunk): when `PF_EVENT_PROJECTION_DIR` is set, `projPath := filepath.Join(projRoot, "events.jsonl")` drops the tenant segment entirely — the env is process-wide and cannot vary per tenant, so every tenant regenerates the *same* file and each append overwrites other tenants' projections (cross-tenant leak + lost projection). Tenant must be joined in both branches.
MAJOR: AC-1 (eventstore.go hunk): retry match narrowed from `"duplicate key"` to `"events_pkey"`. The design mandates retry on the `UNIQUE(tenant_id, seq)` conflict, which is a *separate* constraint unless the PK is exactly `(tenant_id, seq)`; if not, concurrent seq conflicts now abort instead of retrying while PK duplicates retry 5×. No test proves the retry still fires for the actual seq constraint name.

AC-4 observability (delta touches this line): `EnforceOutboxBound` is now invoked, but the rejection still emits no metric/log/counter and the bound check itself produces no row-count signal, so operators cannot distinguish `EVENT_OUTBOX_BOUND_EXCEEDED` backpressure from a generic append failure.
MINOR: Bound check runs *after* payload offload (`payloads.Put` precedes it): an outbox-bound rejection orphans an already-uploaded object and relies on GC grace; the cheap check should fail fast before the expensive write.

Per-append `EnforceOutboxBound` adds a DB round-trip (likely a COUNT over outbox) to every outbox-enabled append: O(pending rows) latency at scale, TOCTOU-racy outside the tx (bound advisory under concurrency), with no supporting index/metric evidence.

`WithOutboxBound` mutates the receiver in place (unsafe if applied to a shared/global store; post-construction config mutation) and silently ignores `<=0`, contradicting the config contract's `invalid_behavior: fail closed`.
New `TestAppendEnforcesOutboxBound` asserts only `err != nil`; an `ErrEventInvalid` or DB error would satisfy it — assert the specific bound error to prove AC-4 backpressure.

`NewEventStore` hard-codes `inlineLimit: 32*1024` / `outboxMax: 100_000` as magic numbers rather than sourcing the declared `EVENT_INLINE_PAYLOAD_LIMIT` / outbox bound from the config contract with startup validation (divergence risk between code and contract).
`PF_EVENT_PROJECTION_DIR` is a new env var read via `os.Getenv` per append, with no startup validation and no entry in the config contract or env registry.

Projection default root `filepath.Join("products", tenant)` is cwd-relative (a service started elsewhere writes where no reader looks, silently stale), and `tenant` is joined unsanitized — a tenant value containing a separator or `..` escapes the projection root.
NIT: The outbox-bound test belongs in `eventstore_test.go`, not `event_outbox_gc_test.go`.
`projection_error` is surfaced only in the returned map; nothing logs/meters it, so AC-3 stale-projection marking depends entirely on callers echoing the field.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly resolves the two prior blockers (caller-controlled projection path now server-resolved; large payload without store now fails closed) and wires `EnforceOutboxBound` into `Append`.

Top risks: the new `PF_EVENT_PROJECTION_DIR` branch drops tenant scoping (blocker), and narrowing the duplicate-match to `events_pkey` may disable the required per-tenant seq retry with no test evidence.
Remaining hardening: bound-check ordering/observability, config-registry alignment for new constants/env var, and stronger assertions in the new tests.

BLOCKER: AC-3 regression (pfcore hunk): with `projRoot == ""` the code still sets `projRoot = filepath.Join("products", tenant)`, and the new line then joins `tenant` again — default writes become `products/<tenant>/<tenant>/events.jsonl`, so existing readers of `products/<tenant>/events.jsonl` silently stop receiving updates (stale projection).
MAJOR: The tenant-path fix (disposition of prior BLOCKER) ships with no test in this delta: nothing asserts the env-set path `<dir>/<tenant>/events.jsonl` nor that the default path stays exactly where legacy readers look, so the double-tenant defect above is undetected by CI.
MINOR: `EnforceOutboxBound` observability fix is log-only (`log.Printf` to stderr, no logger injection/level/structured fields, no `outbox_rows_current`-style metric), so AC-4 row-count limits remain hard to alert on across instances.

The retry hunk still matches constraint names by substring on `err.Error()` (`events_tenant_id_seq_key`); DB error-message coupling is brittle across PG versions/upgrades (pre-existing pattern, extended here).
NIT: The new log line duplicates the `pending=/max=` data already present in the returned error string.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly targets all three prior pending findings, but the AC-3 tenant-path fix is wrong on the default branch (tenant joined twice), breaking legacy `events.jsonl` readers — a hard AC-3 regression.
Outbox bound logging and seq-conflict retry additions look correct but are untested in this delta.
Must fix path composition (append `tenant` only when `projRoot` comes from the env override) and add a regression test for both branches before merge.

MINOR: `projectionPath` joins the raw `tenant` into a filesystem path with no sanitization; a tenant value containing `..` or a separator can escape `PF_EVENT_PROJECTION_DIR`/`products` (tenant is server-resolved, so low likelihood, but this is a new path-construction helper and deserves a boundary assertion).
SUMMARY: Delta resolves the prior BLOCKER (double-tenant default path) and MAJOR (missing tests): `projectionPath` now yields `products/<tenant>/events.jsonl` by default and `<dir>/<tenant>/events.jsonl` under env, matching legacy reader locations, with both cases unit-tested.
Behavior under env-set root is byte-identical to the old code, so AC-3 reader compatibility is preserved; no new AC/security regression introduced.
Residual risk is limited to unsanitized tenant segment in the new path helper (MINOR hardening).
